notes:
The task is to pack 11 unit regular hexagons inside a regular hexagon, minimizing the side length of the outer hexagon.
The seed program uses a fixed lattice arrangement (a "flower" shape with 1 center, 6 neighbors, and 4 from the next ring) and optimizes the position, rotation, and size of the outer hexagon via Linear Programming (LP).
The LP formulation is:
Minimize $S$ (side length of outer hexagon)
Subject to: For all inner hexagon centers $p_i$ and outer hexagon normals $n_k$:
$| (p_i - c) \cdot n_k | + APOTHEM \le S \cdot APOTHEM$
where $c$ is the center of the outer hexagon, $APOTHEM = \sqrt{3}/2$.
This simplifies to:
$| (p_i - c) \cdot n_k | \le (S - 1) APOTHEM$.

The seed program optimizes the rotation $\beta$ of the outer hexagon and the center $c$ for a fixed set of inner hexagon centers $p_i$.
